title: LRU-aware zipper batcher for seqlen cohorting and kernel-cost smoothing
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces the zipper batcher: a seqlen-aware batching heuristic that reduces padding overhead and improves KV cache locality. Default rollout gated by a runtime flag; measurable cost and tail-latency improvements on benchmark workloads.
description: Summary: Add a new 'zipper' batching algorithm that forms cohorts by interleaving short and long sequences (zippering) while biasing selection toward requests with warm KV cache entries (LRU score) and stable kernel-cost profiles. Motivation: Traditional bucketing or pure seqlen-first packing either wastes tokens (padding) or causes frequent kernel-path switching and KV cache churn. The zipper approach aims to reduce padding overhead without scattering requests that would evict hot KV cache lines, and to smooth kernel selection transitions so the runtime can reuse optimized kernels longer. Design: 1) Each incoming request is annotated with sequence_length, lru_score (derived from per-request cache footprint and last-access timestamp), and an estimated kernel_cost vector (small fingerprint mapping to an internal kernel profile). 2) The batcher maintains short and long shelves; instead of flushing full buckets, it pulls from both shelves in zipper order: short,long,short,long,... up to target batch_size or pad-overhead budget. 3) When choosing the next candidate, zipper_batcher scores candidates by combined metric: score = alpha*pad_savings_estimate + beta*lru_preservation + gamma*kernel_cost_alignment. Parameters alpha/beta/gamma are tunable via config; defaults chosen to prioritize pad savings but penalize negative LRU impact. 4) If a potential zipper cohort would change the dominant kernel path for the batch beyond a threshold, the cohorter will bias toward same-kernel candidates or split into two sub-batches to avoid kernel thrash. 5) Integrated backpressure: if latency SLOs start degrading, zipper reduces cohorting aggressiveness and favors immediate flush. Implementation details: - New module src/runtime/batcher/zipper_batcher.rs implementing the heuristic, exposing a runtimeflag enable_zipper and config knobs (alpha,beta,gamma,pad_budget_pct,max_kernel_switch_per_batch). - Added cost-model hook in src/runtime/scheduler/cost_model.rs to return a compact kernel profile id for active models. - KV-awareness surfaced via an LRU-proxy in serving/kv_cache/eviction_policy.rs that produces a per-request lru_score without changing eviction semantics (read-only view). - Small changes in runtime/batcher/mod.rs to register zipper option and wiring into continuous batching loop. - Tests and benchmarks added: tests/perf/zipper_benchmark.py and tests/unit/test_zipper_cohorting.rs. Performance: Benchmarked on A100 and H100 medium/long tail workloads. Representative results vs current default cohorter using 8-shard 40b model: average token cost -11.8%, throughput +17.6% under mixed seqlen traffic, median latency ~unchanged, 95th tail latency -5.1%. When combined with KV-friendly routing these gains improved to token cost -14.2% and tail -8.0%. We also saw a ~10% reduction in kernel-switch events, leading to more stable GPU utilization. Commits: - feat(batcher): zipper batcher core algorithm and config - perf(scheduler): kernel profile id and cost smoothing hook - infra(kv): add lru_score proxy view (read-only) - test(perf): zipper benchmark harness - docs: operator guide and rollout notes Changed files (high level): src/runtime/batcher/zipper_batcher.rs, src/runtime/batcher/mod.rs, src/runtime/scheduler/cost_model.rs, src/serving/kv_cache/eviction_policy.rs, tests/perf/zipper_benchmark.py, docs/operators/zipper-batcher.md Testing and CI: Initial CI run failed integration perf (bench harness timeout) on first push due to lock ordering in LRU proxy. Fixed by introducing a read-lock pattern and adding a stress test. Final CI: unit tests pass, perf harness runs in CI microbench, e2e bench on internal infra completed manually. Rollout plan: Feature gated across runtime via enable_zipper flag. Start with 5% of hosted traffic for 24h, monitor pad_overhead, kernel_switch_events, kv_miss_rate. If metrics stable, ramp to 50% then full. Observability: added metrics zipper_cohort_size, zipper_pad_savings_pct, zipper_kernel_switch_count, zipper_lru_impact_score, and a tracing tag for cohort_id to link traces. Backwards compatibility and safety: zipper is off by default; no changes to on-disk artifacts; LRU proxy is read-only so no cache semantics change. Migration: none required. Review conversation: - Evan Rogers: "Nice idea. Please add a hard safety cap to avoid pathological cohorts that exceed pad budget under bursty short-sequence arrival." Author reply: "Added pad_budget_pct config and enforced at selection time; default 12%" - Priya Singh: "Concerned about kernel switching heuristics; will this hurt tail latency for long conversation workloads?" Author reply: "We added a kernel_switch_threshold and sub-batching path; if threshold exceeded we prefer split batches which preserves tail SLAs." - Luca Moretti: "Please add more unit tests around concurrency with the LRU proxy." Author reply: "Added stress unit test that surfaced lock ordering bug, addressed and documented." Approvals and merge: After two follow-up fixes and CI green, PR approved by Priya Singh and Luca Moretti. Merge method: squash and merge. Related work: complements ENG-4021 (batching cost model refactor) and ENG-4087 (kv-cache telemetry). Notes: This PR purposefully trades a bit more scheduler complexity for measurable token savings and more stable kernel utilization. Operator docs added with guidance and sample config. Known limitations: very high variance seqlen workloads with adversarial arrival patterns still benefit from explicit seqlen bucketing; zipper should be used as a middle-ground heuristic. Future work: adaptive alpha/beta tuning from live metrics and auto-rollout suggestions in optimize service.
